Current (2026) Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, since 13 March 2026; previously LG of Delhi (2022-2026) (Chapter 6)

Education reformer, engineer and climate activist; inspiration for the 'Phunsukh Wangdu' character in the film '3 Idiots'; pioneer of the 'ice stupa' innovation; leading figure of the statehood/Sixth Schedule movement, including the 2024 'Delhi Chalo' padayatra and 2025 hunger strike/NSA detention (Chapters 7, 8)
Influential 20th-century Ladakhi Buddhist monk, statesman and diplomat; served as India's Ambassador to Mongolia; a major figure in modern Ladakhi Buddhist religious and political life

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Sonam Wangchuk's association with the '3 Idiots' character 'Phunsukh Wangdu' is a frequently cited popular-culture fact that helps anchor his broader significance as an educator-turned-activist — useful context alongside his more exam-critical role in the Sixth Schedule/statehood movement.

items: Ladakh: approx 59,146 sq km — India's LARGEST UT by area; population density approx 3/sq km — LOWEST of any Indian state/UT.
2 districts: Leh and Kargil; borders J&K (UT), Himachal Pradesh, LoC (Pakistan) and LAC (China).
Trans-Himalayan ranges: Great Himalaya/Zanskar -> Zanskar Range -> Ladakh Range -> Karakoram (Siachen Glacier).
Indus = defining river; Pangong Tso (partly in China), Tso Moriri (Ramsar site) = key lakes.
Climate = 'cold desert' — extreme aridity + extreme cold; agriculture depends on glacier/snowmelt irrigation.
Namgyal dynasty (founded late 15th/early 16th century) ruled independent Ladakh for ~4 centuries; Senge Namgyal built Leh Palace (predates Potala Palace).
Zorawar Singh conquered Ladakh for the Dogras in 1834 (12 years before the 1846 Treaty of Amritsar).
Treaty of Chushul (1842) confirmed Dogra sovereignty over Ladakh after the failed 1841 Tibet campaign.
31 October 2019: Ladakh becomes a separate UT (no Assembly) under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019.
No Legislative Assembly; administered by an LG. Current LG: Vinai Kumar Saxena (since 13 March 2026).
LAHDC Leh (1995) and LAHDC Kargil (2003): elected local self-government bodies, each headed by a Chief Executive Councillor.
Sixth Schedule (Art. 244(2)/275(1)) currently covers only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; Ladakh's inclusion needs a constitutional amendment.
Twin demands: statehood (~30-member Assembly) + Sixth Schedule protection; also 2 separate Lok Sabha seats (vs current 1 combined) and a Ladakh PSC.
Sept 2025 Leh violence (4 deaths) -> Wangchuk's NSA detention (26 Sept 2025) -> release (14 March 2026) is the key recent timeline.
Tourism, Pashmina wool (Changthang), and defence-related activity are the leading economic sectors.
Leh district: Buddhist-majority; Kargil district: Shia Muslim-majority; both very high Scheduled Tribe population share.
Hemis Monastery (largest/wealthiest) and Thiksey Monastery (Potala-Palace-like) are the flagship gompas.
Hemis Festival (Guru Padmasambhava, masked Cham dances) and Losar (Buddhist New Year) are the key festivals.
Ladakh uniquely borders BOTH the LoC (Pakistan) and LAC (China).
Siachen Glacier: Indian-controlled since Operation Meghdoot (1984), world's highest/largest militarised glacier.
Galwan Valley clash (June 2020): most serious India-China border incident in decades.
Hemis National Park: India's largest national park by area, premier snow leopard habitat.
Revise this chapter last — it consolidates every numeric/name/date fact from Chapters 1-13 in one place for rapid recall.

The single most important LIVE current-affairs topic for Ladakh as of 2026: the still-unresolved statehood/Sixth Schedule demand, following the September 2025 violence and Sonam Wangchuk's detention/release — always check the latest developments closer to your exam date.
This book should be read alongside the companion Jammu & Kashmir GS volume, since both UTs share pre-2019 history, the 2019 reorganisation process, and the Northern Command military theatre.
